_scenario: Two PhysicsWorlds — one "2d" on Rapier2dAdapter, one "3d" on Rapier3dAdapter — tracked on ONE PhysicsSystem inside ONE Application, stepped 600 clean fixed frames of 1/60 s (10 s, exactly one fixed step each, nothing dropped). Each half is built by the same function: a static floor whose top is y = 0, a three-box dynamic stack at x = -1.2 taking §23's density-derived mass path, a 1 kg ball dropped from y = 3 at x = 1.6, a static §24 sensor slab centred (1.6, 1.5) that the ball falls through, and a "kinematic-position" slab swept along X at 0.4 m/s from x = -5 whose target is written onto its node before every frame. Host script applies a §26 impulse of (0.3, 4.5, 0) N·s to each ball on frame 200 through RigidBody.applyImpulse (the command buffer the world drains at the top of that step). The per-step digest is the D6 FNV-1a hash of the pair (world2d.checksum(), world3d.checksum()) in that order — §33's own checksums are the digest inputs, not a re-derivation — and summaryDigest is the same hasher over all 600 per-step digests in step order.
_tier: same-runtime (§33). Rapier is compiled WebAssembly, so its arithmetic does not vary with the host JS engine's Math library — but cross-platform determinism is NOT claimed here: values cross the JS/wasm boundary as f64 → f32, the wasm image is pinned per platform by the package manager, and §33's cross-platform tier requires evidence this suite does not gather. The checksum algorithm itself is exact and cross-platform; only its inputs are runtime-bound.
